title: The Fall Edit
note: Three pieces that earned it. Chosen for the cut first, then held to the same composition standard as everything else here.

picks.note: One hundred percent wool and unlined, so what you feel against you is the wool itself.
One hundred percent virgin wool in a yarn dyed plaid, cut and sewn in Los Angeles.
Full suede and unlined. It will soften and darken where you wear it most.

heading: We read the label so you don’t have to.
body: Every piece here has been through the same check. Shell composition and lining composition, pulled apart, parsed into percentages, and shown on the card before you click anything. No scrolling to the bottom of a product page to find out what you are actually buying.

title: Low, Mid, High
note: A collar, a short button placket and a close fit. The same idea at three prices, so you can see where the money goes. Mostly it goes to the fiber.

picks.label: Low
picks.note: Seventy percent cotton, thirty percent cashmere, in a rib with contrast tipping.

picks.label: Mid
picks.note: One hundred percent cashmere, cut close through the body and the sleeve.

picks.label: High
picks.note: One hundred percent cashmere in a softer, easier shape.

heading: The lining is where it hides.
body: A wool crepe dress with a polyester lining breathes like polyester. Most sites fold the lining into one composition line, or leave it off entirely. We show it separately on every card, and you can filter on it.

title: This Moment: Fringe
note: Fringe is back on knits, coats and skirts. These are leather, wool and cashmere all the way through, so the movement comes from the material itself.

picks.note: Seventy percent wool, thirty percent cashmere, with fringe across the back and down the sleeves.
One hundred percent leather, fringe included. The lining is lyocell, and it says so below.
Wool and cashmere and unlined, with fringe that moves when you walk.

title: Same Shell, Different Lining
by: One brand, one name, two answers
note: Sea New York's Michaela coat and Michaela cape share a name and a one hundred percent wool shell. The coat is lined in polyester and viscose. The cape is lined in cotton. Sea publishes both, and we put it on the front of the card.

picks.note: Wool shell, lined in polyester and viscose. Nothing about the outside tells you that.
The same wool, lined in cotton. It breathes all the way through.
A third answer. Wool flannel lined in acetate and modal, both plant derived, at three hundred fifty dollars.

title: What Silk Looks Like
by: Three pieces that are what they look like
note: Satin is a weave, not a fiber, and most of what is sold as satin is polyester or viscose. These three are silk all the way through, which is what the word used to promise.
cta: See what one hundred percent looks like

picks.note: Four ply silk, heavy enough to hang straight. One hundred percent.
Silk cut on the bias, which is why it moves the way satin is supposed to.
One hundred percent silk, unlined, in ivory.

heading: Natural is not the same as sustainable.
body: Composition tells you how a garment will feel, wear and age. It does not tell you how the animal was treated, who sewed it, or what the dye house released. Those are real questions and we do not pretend a percentage answers them.
